extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians working in arithmetic geometry and readers of Mochizuki's IUT theory
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, structural properties, and algorithmic construction rules for D-/F-prime-strips, bridges, Hodge theatres, poly-isomorphisms, LabCusp classes, automorphism subgroups, and radial environments in the IUT framework. Focuses on how these objects are formed, related, and transformed (torsor/automorphism structure, transport of label classes, functorial algorithms, multiradial/uniradial notions).

rubrics_metrics.name: LabCusp(cid:6)(yDv) — (cid:6)-label classes of cusps
rubrics_metrics.description: For v in V, a (cid:6)-label class of cusps of yDv is the set of cusps of yDv lying over a single cusp of yD(cid:6)_v (for v in Varc considered as the set of cusps of yDv or yD(cid:6)_v). LabCusp(cid:6)(yDv) denotes the set of (cid:6)-label classes and has a natural F_l-action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithmically reconstructable (Corollary 6.12, Corollary 2.9) from group-theoretic data; LabCusp(yDv) has a natural F_l-group structure, admits a zero element y^0_v and a canonical element y^(cid:6)_v defined up to multiplication by mu_{l}, and there is a natural bijection LabCusp(cid:6)(yDv) ≃ F_l (well-defined up to multiplication by mu_{l}) compatible with prior bijections (Proposition 10.15). The F_l-group structure gives a surjection Aut(yDv) → mu_{l} by induced automorphism on LabCusp; the kernel is Aut+(yDv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aut+(yDv) and Aut^-(yDv) — positive and negative automorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Aut+(yDv) := kernel of the surjection Aut(yDv) → mu_{l} induced by action on LabCusp(cid:6)(yDv). Aut^(cid:0)(yDv) := Aut(yDv) ∩ Aut+(yDv) is referred to as the set/subgroup of negative automorphisms in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aut+(yDv) are the 'positive' automorphisms stabilising the LabCusp label class structure; splitting Aut into positive/negative parts is used to define +-full poly-isomorphisms and to control torsor actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed automorphism subgroups Aut+(yD) and Aut^{(eps)}(yD)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sign vector (cid:11) ∈ {±1}^V (or f(cid:6)1g_V), Aut+(yD) (resp. Aut^{(cid:11)}(yD)) denotes the subgroup of automorphisms whose v-component is positive (resp. has sign (cid:11)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These subgroups organise automorphisms componentwise across v∈V and are used to define signed +-full poly-automorphisms and to control compatibility of poly-morphisms across components.

rubrics_metrics.name: +-full poly-isomorphism / +-full poly-automorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: A +-full poly-isomorphism yDv (cid:24)(cid:0)! zDv is a poly-isomorphism obtained as the Aut+(yDv)-orbit (or equivalently Aut+(zDv)-orbit) of a given poly-isomorphism. If yD = zD, the set of +-full poly-isomorphisms yDv → yDv has a natural bijection with {±1}^V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The +-full poly-isomorphism determined by the identity automorphism is called positive; the other one(s) are called negative. For a sign vector (cid:11) the corresponding (cid:11)-signed +-full poly-isomorphism is defined analogously. Capsule-+-full poly-morphisms are collections of such +-full poly-isomorphisms indexed by capsule components; signs and orbits under Aut+ control indeterminacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capsule-+-full poly-morphism between capsules of D-prime-strips
rubrics_metrics.description: A capsule-+-full poly-morphism between capsules fyDt_g∈T and fzDt0_g∈T0 is a collection of +-full poly-isomorphisms yDt (cid:19): T → T0, relative to some injection, i.e., compatible collections of +-full poly-isomorphisms between corresponding components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to glue or compare capsules of D-prime-strips; compatibility conditions (injections of index sets) and Aut+-orbits control uniqueness and torsor structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outer homomorphism Aut(D^(cid:6)) → GL2(F_l)/{±1} and associated subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: From the model global object D^(cid:6) one can group-theoretically construct an outer homomorphism Aut(D^(cid:6)) → GL2(F_l)/{±1} whose image contains the Borel subgroup of SL2(F_l)/{±1}. The rank one quotient yields a natural surjective homomorphism Aut(D^(cid:6)) → F_l^*; write Aut^{(cid:6)}(D^(cid:6)) for the kernel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aut^{(cid:6)}(D^(cid:6)) contains Aut_K(X_K) and acts transitively on cusps of X_K. The subgroup Aut_cusp(D^(cid:6)) (fixing cusps) can be reconstructed group-theoretically and fits into natural outer isomorphisms Aut_K(X_K) ≃ Aut^{(cid:6)}(D^(cid:6))/Aut_cusp(D^(cid:6)) ≃ F_l^* (choice of cusp dependent). These structures induce F_l-group and F_l-torsor actions used later in evaluation maps and symmetry discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model D-(cid:2)(cid:6)-Bridge (Definition 10.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: A construction regarding D-prime-strips D_v indexed by v∈V and copies indexed by t∈F_l forming D^(cid:31) = {D_v;v∈V} and tautological D-prime-strip families Dt for each t∈F_l; positive +-full poly-isomorphisms (cid:30)(cid:2)(cid:6)_t : D_vt → D^(cid:31);v produce a model base-(D)-(cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge D^(cid:6) := {D_t}_t∈F_l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a natural poly-automorphism of order 2 (acting by multiplication by −1 on F_l) and further compatibilities with sign vectors (cid:11)∈{±1}^V producing poly-automorphisms of the triple (D^(cid:6); D^(cid:31); identifications). These model objects serve as templates for base-bridges and for defining actions of Fo(cid:6)_l on index sets and components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model D-(cid:2)ell-Bridge (Definition 10.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analogous to Definition 10.30 but where F_l is regarded as an F_l-torsor; Dt = {D_vt}_v∈V for each t∈F_l and D^(cid:6) := {Dt}_t∈F_l; poly-morphisms are constructed equivariantly under Aut_cusp(D^(cid:6)) and produce model base-(D)-(cid:2)ell-bridges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction yields natural poly-actions of Fo(cid:6)_l and produces poly-automorphisms equivariant with respect to these actions; used to pass between torsor-indexed capsules and model global objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-(D)-(cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge (Definition 10.32 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A base-(D)-(cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge is a poly-morphism y(cid:30)(cid:2)(cid:6) : yDT → yD^(cid:31) where yDT is a capsule of D-prime-strips indexed by an F_l-group T and yD^(cid:31) is a D-prime-strip, with an isomorphism of index sets Fl ≃ T induced by conjugation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isomorphisms of such bridges consist of compatible pairs (on capsules and global D-prime-strips) respecting F_l-group structure and +-full poly-isomorphisms; compositions defined naturally. Index torsor/group and conjugation actions are part of the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-(D)-(cid:2)ell-bridge (Definition 10.32 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A poly-morphism y(cid:30)(cid:2)ell : yDT → yD^(cid:6) where yD^(cid:6) is a category equivalent to the model global object and yDT is a capsule indexed by an F_l-torsor T, with identifications of index sets as F_l-torsors and conjugation compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isomorphisms involve Aut_cusp(yD^(cid:6))-orbits of capsule-+-full poly-isomorphisms; used to induce poly-morphisms Dt_t → yD^(cid:6) parametrized by t∈T.

rubrics_metrics.name: D-(cid:1)-Hodge theatre (Definition 10.32 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection yHT D-(cid:1) = (yD^(cid:31), y(cid:30)(cid:2), yDT, y(cid:30)(cid:2)ell : yDT → yD^(cid:6)) where y(cid:30)(cid:2) is a D-(cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge, y(cid:30)(cid:2)ell is a D-(cid:2)(cid:6)ell-bridge, and there are isomorphisms between model global objects identifying the pieces appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An isomorphism of D-(cid:1)-Hodge theatres is a pair of isomorphisms of the respective D-(cid:2)ell-bridges and D-(cid:2)(cid:6)-bridges inducing the same poly-isomorphism on capsules; compositions defined in the obvious manner. Serves as the multiplicative+additive combined structure in IUT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport of (cid:6)-Label Classes via Base-Bridges (Proposition 10.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-(cid:1)-Hodge theatre, the D-(cid:2)ell-bridge y(cid:30)(cid:2)ell induces isomorphisms y^(cid:16)_(cid:2)ell_vt : LabCusp(cid:6)(yD_vt) → LabCusp(cid:6)(yD^(cid:6)) (F_l-torsors) for each v∈V, t∈T; composites between v and w are F_l-group isomorphisms and identifications across v produce a single common LabCusp structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The D-(cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge similarly induces isomorphisms LabCusp(cid:6)(yD_vt) → LabCusp(cid:6)(yD^(cid:31);v). By varying v one writes LabCusp(cid:6)(yD_t) and these isomorphisms are compatible, giving canonical identifications and an overall torsor isomorphism y^(cid:16)_(cid:6) : LabCusp(cid:6)(yD^(cid:6)) → T (F_l-torsors). Actions by Aut_cusp and substitutions by signed automorphisms are described and tracked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of D-(cid:2)(cid:6)-Bridges / D-(cid:2)ell-Bridges / D-(cid:1)-Hodge theatres (Proposition 10.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various torsor and equivariance properties: (1) For a D-(cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge the set Isom(y(cid:30)(cid:2)(cid:6), z(...)) is an {±1} × {±1}^V-torsor where the first factor corresponds to the (cid:0)1Fl automorphism and the second to sign vectors. (2) For D-(cid:2)ell-bridges Isom sets are Fo(cid:6)_l-torsors and naturally isomorphic. (3) For D-(cid:1)-Hodge theatres Isom sets are {±1}-torsors with a natural identification. (4),(5) Further torsor descriptions and existence of functorial algorithms to construct D-(cid:1)-Hodge theatres from D-(cid:2)ell-bridges up to Fo(cid:6)-indeterminacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These torsor descriptions control the indeterminacies and the nature of isomorphism classes; they specify which finite groups act transitively on isomorphism sets and thereby quantify the non-uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: D-(cid:1)-link / base-(D)-(cid:2)(cid:6)ell-link (Definition 10.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: A base-(D)-(cid:2)(cid:6)ell-link (or D-(cid:1)-link) between D-(cid:1)-Hodge theatres yHT and zHT is the full poly-isomorphism yD' → zD' between the mono-analyticisations of the D-prime-strips constructed (Lemma 10.38).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a D-(cid:1)-link the D'-prime-strips are shared but not the arithmetically holomorphic structures. The (cid:19)etale-picture visualises 'shared' vs 'non-shared' relation and allows permutation symmetry; this is used to compare theatres while keeping holomorphic/an arithmetic structure distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: (cid:2)(cid:6)-Bridge, (cid:2)ell-Bridge, (cid:1)-Hodge theatre over F-prime-strips (Definition 10.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: (cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge is a poly-morphism yFT → zF^(cid:31) where yFT is a capsule of F-prime-strips indexed by an F_l-group T lifting a D-(cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge. A (cid:2)ell-bridge lifts D-(cid:2)ell-bridges via F-prime-strips indexed by an F_l-torsor; a (cid:1)-Hodge theatre collects (cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge and (cid:2)ell-bridge with matching associated D-objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are lifts to the F-side (arithmetic side) of the D-side constructions. Isomorphisms of such objects must lift the associated D-bridges and respect the lifts; they are used to perform arithmetic constructions and to compare multiplicative/additive data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism bijectivity and torsor lifting properties (Lemma 10.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: For pairs of (cid:2)(cid:6)-bridges / (cid:2)ell-bridges / (cid:1)-Hodge theatres whose associated D-objects coincide, the natural map from Isom on lifted (F-)objects to Isom on associated D-objects is bijective. Also the set of capsule-+-full poly-isomorphisms making a pair form a (cid:1)-Hodge theatre is an Fo(cid:6)_l × {±1}^V-torsor with the first factor corresponding to Fo(cid:6)_l structure group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lemma clarifies that lifting to F-side does not create extra ambiguity beyond the prescribed torsor actions and that isomorphisms are controlled by the D-side data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial algorithm from D-(cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge to D-(cid:2)-bridge (Lemma 10.38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-(cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge y(cid:30)(cid:2)(cid:6) (or (cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge), there is an algorithmic procedure: form the quotient jTj = T/{±1}, identify components in fibers via the quotient, obtain l-capsule yD_jTj and the D-prime-strip yD^> (non-zero part), replace +-full poly-morphisms by full poly-morphisms at v∈Vgood, and replace +-full by evaluation-section-determined poly-morphisms at v∈Vbad. The output is a functorially obtained D-(cid:2)-bridge yDT^> : yDT^> → yD^>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure is algorithmic and functorial; the steps show how to remove ±1-index indeterminacy and to pass from +-full to full poly-morphisms depending on local type (good/bad/arc). This is a key step enabling later gluing and mono-analyticisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing uniqueness and recognition via functorial algorithm (Definition 10.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a (cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge yFT has associated D-(cid:2)(cid:6)-bridge yDT and the functorial algorithm constructs a D-(cid:2)-bridge yDT^> lying over yDT, then any (cid:2)-bridge zFJ whose D-part zD^> lies over yDT^> is regarded as constructed via the functorial algorithm; the gluing isomorphism is unique (Proposition 10.20 (2), Lemma 10.25 (1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies when an F-side object should be considered as arising from the D-side functorial construction and asserts uniqueness of the gluing isomorphism, which controls how local pieces assemble into global theatres.

rubrics_metrics.name: D-(cid:2)(cid:1)-Hodge Theatre and (cid:2)(cid:6)ellNF-Hodge theatre (Definition 10.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: A base-/D- D-(cid:2)(cid:6)ellNF-Hodge theatre yHT D-(cid:2)(cid:1) is a triple: a D-(cid:2)-Hodge theatre, a D-(cid:1)-Hodge theatre, and the (necessarily unique) gluing isomorphism between them. Similarly a (cid:2)(cid:6)ellNF-Hodge theatre is the analogue on the (cid:2)-side and the (cid:1)-side with unique gluing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions combine multiplicative (D-(cid:2)) and additive (D-(cid:1)) portions into full Hodge theatres by specifying the unique gluing, formalising the arithmetic-analytic hybrid objects used in evaluation maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radial Environment (Definition 11.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A radial environment is a triple (R, C, (cid:8)) where R,C are groupoids with all objects isomorphic and (cid:8): R → C is an essentially surjective functor. C is called coric category (objects coric data), R radial category (objects radial data), and (cid:8) a radial algorithm (mutations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended as a formalisation of species/mutations: (cid:8) is expected to be algorithmically defined. One considers R/C diagrams, corically defined lifts, graphs of functors Graph((cid:4)) for auxiliary functors, and compatibilities of indexings. This notion is used to describe how algorithm contents (radial data) map to coric data and to control liftability of isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial vs Uniradial (Definition 11.1 (2),(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: (cid:8) is multiradial iff (cid:8) is full; uniradial iff (cid:8) is not full. A multiradial environment (R,C,(cid:8)) is one where (cid:8) is multiradial; uniradial environment when not full. (cid:9)_R : R → yR is multiradially/uniradially defined when compatible with (cid:8) and the diagram R → yR → C commutes up to 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If (cid:8) is uniradial, isomorphisms in C need not lift to R (loss of rigidity, additional indeterminacy). Multiradiality ensures liftability of isomorphisms enabling a kind of parallel transport between radial data via coric data; used crucially in the final multiradial algorithm to 'switch' theta values up to controlled indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph((cid:4)) and corically defined functors (Definition 11.1 (4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given (cid:4): R → E another functor, Graph((cid:4)) is the category of pairs (R, (cid:4)(R)) with morphisms pairs (f, (cid:4)(f)). There is a commutative diagram of natural functors relating R, Graph((cid:4)), and C via (cid:8) and the induced Graph((cid:4)) functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graph construction used to formalise interplay between radial data and auxiliary functor images; corically defined means (cid:9)_R factors through C via (cid:4)_R so that diagram commutes, expressing that a radial construction is in fact determined by coric data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Switching functor property and consequence of multiradiality (Remark 11.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a radial environment (R,C,(cid:8)) write R(2)_C R for triples (R1,R2,(cid:11): (cid:8)(R1) ≅ (cid:8)(R2)). The switching functor (R1,R2,(cid:11)) ↦ (R2,R1,(cid:11)^{-1}) preserves isomorphism classes of objects in R(2)_C R if (cid:8) is multiradial, since any (R1,R2,(cid:11)) is isomorphic to (R1,R1,id).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiradiality therefore permits 'switching' two radial data up to isomorphism, a key combinatorial symmetry used in the final multiradial algorithm to permute theta-values (with controlled mild indeterminacies). This switching underlies upper bounds on height functions via inability to distinguish certain pilot objects up to indeterminacies (Indet ", Indet !, Indet xy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: holomorphic structures as radial environment (Example 11.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classical example: R = category of 1-dimensional C-vector spaces and C = category of 2-dimensional R-vector spaces, with (cid:8) forgetting complex structure (sending 1-dim C-vector spaces to underlying R^2). This radial environment is uniradial (isomorphisms in C need not lift). If R is replaced by 1-dim C-vector spaces equipped with GL2(R)-orbit of an identification to a fixed R^2, the environment becomes tautologically multiradial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates the difference: uniradiality corresponds to hidden holomorphic structure not visible after forgetting, while multiradiality corresponds to having extra rigidifying data (orbits) ensuring liftability of isomorphisms. Serves as an accessible model for the IUT multiradial/uniradial dichotomy.
